screenshot_findings_after_round1.issue:
The web chat-list preview cuts a signed number in half. The CSS ellipsis keeps the end of the figure and drops its sign and leading digits. The row «محلل الذهب» stores «… وتراجع −1.5% أمس». At 390 it shows «….5%» and at 1280 «…%», in ar and en, light and dark. A reader sees a different, unsigned number (VISION 17 and 0.4). The earlier reversal (finding 0) is fixed, but this truncation replaces it.

Selector: `.thread[data-key="agent:…"] .pv > span[dir]` (SaidLine), styled by `.thread .pv > span { overflow:hidden; text-overflow:ellipsis }` in apps/web/src/shell/lists/lists.css. The group heads-up (HeadsUp.tsx, `.hu-t small > span`) uses the same pattern.

Cause: plainLine wraps each number in LRI…PDI characters. text-overflow clips characters at the end edge of the line, so the LTR run at the left end of an RTL line loses its left part, which is the sign.

Mobile (apps/mobile/components/shell/thread-row.tsx) uses the same isolates with numberOfLines={1}. At 390 its cut happened to fall after the number, so mobile has the same latent defect.
screenshot_findings_after_round1.evidence:
- Screenshots: shots-v38b/web-chats-390x844-{ar,en}-{light,dark}.png and web-chats-1280x800-*.png. The same list appears in every 1280 web shot.
- Zooms: shots-v38b/zoom/web-chats-390-ar-goldrow.png («….5%») and zoom/web-chats-1280-ar-goldrow.png («…%»).
- DOM text: «ربح الحساب (⁦+$239⁩) اليوم وتراجع ⁦−1.5%⁩ أمس» (audit `cut:ellipsis` on `.pv > span`).
- Chrome repro: shots-v38b/zoom/cut-test.png. The top row uses isolates and shows «…%». The bottom row uses an inline-block <bdi> and the whole number is hidden behind the ellipsis.
screenshot_findings_after_round1.fix:
Render each signed number in the preview as an atomic inline, for example <bdi dir="ltr" style="display:inline-block"> in SaidLine and HeadsUp. text-overflow then hides the figure whole rather than in part (checked in Chrome).

On mobile, a nested RN Text cannot be atomic. Make the core line drop a figure that does not fit whole, or test thread-row at narrower widths and apply an equivalent.

Add a chat-lists assertion that a cut preview never shows a partial number.

rereview_findings_round1.issue: On desktop (900px and wider), clicking «Full screen» on any expandable sheet hits «Close» and shuts the sheet. This is a global-area defect from port part 1 (be050c4f, the 44px hit-area rule). It is still present after these fixes, and the fix report says the area is clean. At line 2216, `.sheet-top > .icon { position: static }` (specificity 0,2,0) overrides the zero-specificity `:where(.icon) { position: relative }`. Each icon's absolute `::before` therefore resolves against `.sheet-top`. With `width: max(100%, 44px)` it spans the whole 72px bar, and Close is later in the DOM, so it sits on top of «Full screen». Main de1e2827 has no `max(100%, 44px)` rule, so this regression comes from the port.
rereview_findings_round1.evidence: tests/web/agent-pages.spec.mjs:251 («the chart sheet draws the broker's candles…») fails in both of my runs, rvglobw1 and rvglobw2: `<button class="icon" aria-label="Close"> intercepts pointer events` when clicking «Full screen». A headless-Chrome repro of the same rules (scratchpad/rvglob/meta/sheet.html) also shows elementFromPoint at the expand button's centre returning #close. The fixer's runs never included agent-pages.spec.
rereview_findings_round1.fix: Keep the sheet icons positioned in the ≥900px rule: use `position: relative` instead of `static`. They are already flex items there, so the layout does not change. Pin it in v38-global at 1280: on an expandable sheet, elementFromPoint at the centre of «Full screen» must return that button, and clicking it gives #dialog the class `expanded`.

rereview_findings_round1.issue: The prefix-direction and first-words fix was applied to web ThreadRow, web HeadsUp and mobile thread-row, but not to the mobile heads-up banner. messageBanner still returns `${speaker}: ${content}` as one string. heads-up.tsx renders it in one Text with `writingDirection: "auto"`, which is not a CSS direction, so react-native-web 0.21 falls back to the root Text's dir="auto". As a result, in the Arabic UI a Latin agent name in a group («FX scout: الذهب ارتفع…») makes the whole line left-to-right: the speaker lands on the left and is read last. The numberOfLines={2} cut then falls on the LTR end, which is the start of the Arabic words. The English UI has the mirror-image case.
rereview_findings_round1.evidence: apps/mobile/lib/heads-up.ts:58 joins speaker and content. apps/mobile/components/heads-up.tsx:247-256 has writingDirection "auto" and textAlign by UI. In node_modules/react-native-web/dist/exports/Text/index.js:108 the root Text gets dir='auto'. Web HeadsUp now uses SaidLine for exactly this case, so web and mobile banners differ.
rereview_findings_round1.fix: Return { who, text } from messageBanner, as web's Banner.who does. Render who in the interface's direction and the words in their own writingDirection/textAlign (textDirection), as thread-row's `said` does. Pin it in tests/mobile/heads-up.test.ts and in an Arabic group-banner case in the heads-up spec.

rereview_findings_round1.issue: The new cut can fall inside a signed number and then isolate the fragment as if it were a whole number. The new tsx pin expects this: `${"ر".repeat(117)} +3.1% ثم` cut at 120 gives «… ⁦+3⁩…». In the 120-character snippet (quote and reply bar) and in web and mobile heads-up banners, a trader sees «+3» where the figure is +3.1%. Only the ellipsis signals the cut. This touches VISION 17 (signed numbers read right) and 0.4 (every text true). The old code also cut mid-number, so this is not new, but this change is where the cut became deliberate and pinned.
rereview_findings_round1.evidence: tests/web/plain-line.test.ts: `assert.equal(cut, `${"ر".repeat(117)} ${LRI}+3${PDI}…`)`. plainLine slices at `max` code units with no check for a SIGNED_NUMBER match spanning the boundary.
rereview_findings_round1.fix: When the cut falls inside a SIGNED_NUMBER match (or inside a word), back it off to the start of that token before appending «…». Change the pin to expect the number either dropped whole or kept whole.

rereview_findings_round1.issue: The Latin-bubble alignment fix aligns wrapped lines left, but `.meta` (time and ticks) still has `float: left`. In the Arabic UI, when the last line of a Latin bubble has room, the timestamp sits at the left edge and pushes that line's words to its right («10:21  past two pips.»). The last line is now indented, and the time reads before the words. The same happens today for every LTR bubble in the English UI; v38 has the same `.meta` rule.
rereview_findings_round1.evidence: Headless-Chrome repro of the shipped rules: scratchpad/rvglob/meta/page.html → shot.png. Before the fix, the time is at the far left with the words right-aligned. After it, «10:21 past two pips.» on the last line of a 3-line Latin bubble.
rereview_findings_round1.fix: Float the meta to the end of an LTR text block. For example, `.bubble:has(> .text[dir="ltr"]) > .meta { float: right; margin: 7px 0 -3px 12px }`, plus the same for html[dir=ltr] bubbles. Alternatively, leave it and record that the English-side layout is accepted. Pin the meta's x position against the last line.

rereview_findings_round1.issue: keep_tool_titles throws away titles it already had. Each preview replaces the whole saved set with whatever the server lists right now. So a pinned tool the server stops listing, or now lists with no title, loses its known title. From then on the saved list shows its raw name. Before this change, the reviewed title stayed. D6 says never fall back to a raw name where a title can be known.
rereview_findings_round1.evidence: Line 246: `connection.state = {**(connection.state or {}), "tool_titles": dict(titles)}`, called from the preview route on every preview. That includes the manual «مراجعة الأدوات» on a server whose schema changed (IntegrationsPage shows that button when `!server.trusted_tier || review`), and the sheet's automatic read. Scenario: a server is trusted with titles {A: "Alpha", B: "Beta"}, then drops A. The owner opens Review, and the state becomes {B: "Beta"}. GET /capabilities then gives A no title, and the sheet shows raw `A`, even with a fresh read. trust_source can replace the set because it re-pins the tools at the same time; a preview pins nothing.
rereview_findings_round1.fix: In keep_tool_titles, merge rather than replace: `{**saved_titles, **titles}`, keeping the earlier title for any name this read does not list. Add a pytest pin: save titles, then preview with one tool missing, and /capabilities still returns its title.

rereview_findings_round1.issue: The sheet's automatic read (McpToolRows) runs whenever any trusted tool has no saved title. That includes a tool the server never titles, which stays untitled for good. So every opening of that server's sheet makes a live tools/list call to the remote MCP server with the stored credentials, plus a row-locked write. It also does this for a server the owner switched off: review() never checks `enabled`, and McpToolRows does not look at server.enabled. Before this change, opening a sheet never contacted the server.
rereview_findings_round1.evidence: Line 56: `const missing = saved && tools.some((tool) => toolTitle(titles, tool.name) === undefined);` drives a useEffect that POSTs `/trusted-sources/mcp/{id}/preview`. The settings.spec fixture itself has such a tool (toString, never titled), so its sheet would re-read on every open. apps/api/src/lonora_api/routes/trusted_sources.py review() reads the server without an enabled check.
rereview_findings_round1.fix: Limit the automatic read to the case D6 is about, a server trusted before titles were kept, i.e. `saved && Object.keys(titles).length === 0`. Skip it when `!server.enabled`. The manual «مراجعة الأدوات» stays for everything else.

rereview_findings_round1.issue: Pre-existing, on a line this fix edited: the refused-tools note always joins tool names with the Arabic comma «، », in English too. Mobile's names() uses `rtl ? "، " : ", "`, so the two apps differ.
rereview_findings_round1.evidence: Line 191: `.map((name) => `⁨${toolTitle(preview.titles, name) ?? name}⁩`).join("، ")`. main had the same `.join("، ")` at line 132.
rereview_findings_round1.fix: Join by the interface language (", " in English), as mobile does.

repair_failures_and_lead_decisions: LEAD DECISION 1, the 560px budget is exceeded (VISION 10.1.4): with the 550px approval slot, a card holding it is 650px at rest with its head, so its other blocks always fold. A second slot makes the card fall back. A decided entry card renders up to 706px. Options: shorten the decided approval, record an explicit VISION exception for fixed-card slots, or count the slot by the record's state at compile time.

LEAD DECISION 2 (modify_order not counted): a modify_order approval with its ticket row is taller than the counted entry card. It reaches 580px decided in English, so its card renders at 740px while the compiler estimates it under 720 and never falls it back. Counting 580 would make every approval card about 680px at rest. Recorded in docs/genui.md and genui_compile.py as not counted.

LEAD DECISION 3 (long Secret labels not counted): Secret field labels at the contract's 60-character maximum wrap the form and its saving lines. A 2-field card then reaches 756px (about 916px with its head), which the 720px rule does not catch. Recorded as not counted, like the existing replaces-line limit. Options: cap the labels or count them.
